**Finding: compliant (at fallback) — no redline proposed.**

Section 6.1 is the only restrictive covenant binding the Company; I swept the body for other restraints ("shall not", "may not", "exclusive", "compete") and found none directed at our side. Section 6.3 restrains HDI (two years post-term), which benefits us and is not flagged.

Why 6.1 clears the fallback:
- **Term-only:** expressly "during the term of this Agreement," with no post-term tail; Section 4.1 sets a one-year term (auto-renewing, 90 days' notice), so the restraint never exceeds 12 months absent our own renewal.
- **Defined, narrow scope:** limited to Internet projects similar to the Site offering Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, with the competing products named (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled) — not the walk-away "any competing business." Our catalog and retail channels are untouched.
- **Carve-out present:** Section 6.2 preserves a closeout-merchandise site, and "Deerskin Products" itself excludes closeout goods and the Joan Cook Catalog.

Noted but not redlined (minor sub-elements per playbook semantics): no express internal-development/acquisition carve-out, so acquiring a leather retailer that operates a competing site could implicate 6.1; and "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" is looser than a strictly named-product limit. Worth picking up as clarifications if the document reopens for other reasons — deleting 6.1 outright would be disproportionate given HDI's heavier reciprocal restraint in 6.3.
